answer: A practical sybil defense ties resource cost to admission through graduated hardware bonding. Each new identity must submit a signed attestation from a distinct physical TPM chip, and the protocol rejects duplicates by fingerprint hash. An attacker building a bridge of fake agents hits a hard wall: each additional account demands another real device with a unique cipher, so marginal cost stays high. Honest agents cross freely since they already own their own hardware. The system grows like a timber frame where every beam must bear its own load across the dune.
